topics.title: Principles of biotechnology and the first recombinant DNA

concepts.learning_objective: Describe genetic engineering and bioprocess engineering as the two core techniques of modern biotechnology.
Explain why an alien piece of DNA must be linked to an origin of replication to multiply in a host.
Describe how Cohen and Boyer constructed and cloned the first recombinant DNA.
Explain the naming convention of restriction enzymes and distinguish endonucleases from exonucleases.
Explain how restriction enzymes recognise palindromic sequences and produce sticky ends.

topics.title: Separation and isolation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how agarose gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to size.
Describe how separated DNA bands are visualised and recovered from the gel.
Describe the role of the origin of replication, selectable marker and cloning sites in a vector.
Explain how insertional inactivation is used to select recombinants from non-recombinants.
Explain how disarmed Ti plasmids and retroviruses are used as vectors in plants and animals.

topics.title: Competent host and introducing recombinant DNA into host cells

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how bacterial cells are made competent to take up recombinant DNA.
Distinguish micro-injection, biolistics and disarmed pathogen vectors as methods of gene transfer.
Explain how a selectable marker allows only transformed cells to grow.

topics.title: Isolating and cutting DNA, and amplification by PCR

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the steps used to isolate pure DNA from cells.
Explain the steps of PCR and the role of primers and thermostable DNA polymerase.

topics.title: Obtaining the foreign gene product and downstream processing

concepts.learning_objective: Define a recombinant protein and explain why continuous culture improves yield.
Describe the features and advantages of stirred-tank bioreactors for large-scale production.
Describe the steps of downstream processing before a product is marketed.
